 (Special Original Jurisdiction)
 WEDNESDAY ,THE TENTH DAY OF JULY  TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY FOUR  PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE RAVI CHEEMALAPATI  WRIT PETITION NO: 25318/2022 Between:
Vadisala Srinivasa Rao, and Others ...PETITIONER(S)
 AND The State Of Andhra Pradesh and Others ...RESPONDENT(S)
Counsel for the Petitioner(S):
1. KILARU NITHIN KRISHNA Counsel for the Respondent(S):
1. GP FOR REVENUE 2. GP FOR LAND ACQUISITION The Court made the following:
Sri Ravi Teja Padiri, learned counsel representing learned counsel for the petitioners contended that, the respondents authorities are attempting to dispossess the petitioners from the subject properties, without following the procedure envisaged under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013, duly stating that an award has been passed.

The award passed if any, would be behind the back of the petitioner and the respondents are insisting the petitioners to take compensation as per the said award which was illegally determined by the respondents.
Aggrieved thereby, filed the present writ petition.

He further submitted that, the 4th respondent had issued a notice dated 08.06.2021 asking the petitioners to appear in-person or by authorized agent on 07.07.2021 before the RDO and the said notice was served on the petitioners on 05.07.2021.

The said notice was issued in clear violation of the provisions of Section 21(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Vadisala Srinivasa Rao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132262562/
1 Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'Act, 2013').
In fact, the 5th petitioner had died in the year 2015 and the same was brought to notice of the authorities by way of representation through her LR.

Furthermore, from the contents of the counter, the petitioners' learnt that an award was passed under Section 23 of the Act, 2013 and in the said award, it was mentioned that the said notice was served on the 5th petitioner who had already died in the year 2015.

Before passing an award under Section 23 of the Act, 2013, the authorities have to follow the provisions envisaged under Section 21 and 22 of the Act, 2013 but in the present case, no such procedure was followed which is contrary to the provisions of the Act, 2013.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that, by virtue of the award passed by the authorities, where the physical copy was seen by them after filing counter, the relief sought in the present writ petition has to be amended.
Also, in the cause title, the name of the 5th petitioner was wrongly mentioned instead of her LR's.
The authorities knowing pretty well that, the writ petitions are pending, they are trying to demolish the petitioner's structure.

If the same is allowed to happen,
the petitioners would be put to irreparable loss and hardship and the purpose of filing the writ petition would also be defeated.
As such prayed to pass appropriate orders protecting the interest of the petitioners, pending writ petition.
On the other hand, learned Assistant Government Pleader sought time to submit the case on merits.
A bare reading of the notice dated 08.06.2021 shows that the petitioners were asked to appear in person or by authorized agent on 07.07.2021 before the RDO, Anakapalli.

According to the petitioners, the said notice was served on them on 05.07.2021 leaving two days to appear before the RDO, as against the mandate contained in the statue under Section 21(2) of the Act, 2013, which reads as follows:
(2)The public notice referred to in sub-section (1) shall state the particulars of the land so needed, and require all persons interested in the land to appear personally or by agent or advocate before the Collector at a time and place mentioned in the public notice not being less than thirty days and not more than six months after the date of publication of the notice, and to state the nature of their respective interests in the land and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests, their claims to rehabilitation and resettlement along with their objections,
if any, to the measurements made under section 20.
Also, a perusal of the award passed by the authorities shows that the said notice was issued on 5th petitioner who died in the year 2015.
Whether the said action is legitimate or not, needs to be decided.
As on today, no Government Pleader is appointed to assist this Court by virtue of change in Government.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners, in the meantime, if the petitioners' structures were demolished, they would be put to irreparable loss and hardship and the purpose of filing the writ petition would also be defeated.

Therefore, to strike the balance and to meet the ends of justice, this court is inclined to grant the following interim order:
Vadisala Srinivasa Rao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132262562/
